name: Hall of Femme
_comment_group: One of the shows under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
over it. What makes it this show rather than one of its neighbours is
the face, the colour of the card and the colours the user may swap
between - and nothing else. Everything about how the words are CHOSEN
and SET comes from the two presets below.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: What separates this show from the others under the heading is one
sentence long: it is set in Telegraf, on a hot pink card, in colours
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals, the
shape of the card, where it stands on the frame, what a picked word
does - is the Snapchat caption design and is stated once, in
content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This pack states only what
makes it this show, which is the whole of what a pack under this
That the type can be a hairline at all is a consequence of the card. A
200-weight face over an unknown photograph is the one thing a caption
must never be: on a blown-out sky it disappears, and no drop shadow
saves letters this thin. On a card of its own it has a background
somebody chose, and the weight becomes a choice instead of a risk.

_comment_color: The channel's own answer, and therefore what every frame is set
in until somebody presses a swatch: a frame stores no colour of
its own until it is given one, and this is what it falls back to
(see state.textColorFor). It is one of the four in `colors` below,
so the white swatch is the one that shows as chosen on an
untouched frame - but nothing requires that, and the swatch is
found by matching this value rather than by being listed first.
White letters on the hot pink card is the pairing this show opens
on: the pink is the brand, so it is the CARD - the shape that is a
fifth of the frame and reads before anything on it - and the type
is what has to stay legible against it. The other fifteen pairings
are a button away, black among them.
_comment_colors: The four colours this show is set in, offered for the letters and
for the card behind them - four buttons each in the title panel
The same four in both lists, deliberately. The point is the
PAIRING: sixteen combinations of a hot pink, a butter yellow, a
white and a black, and the ones worth having are the ones that
read. A palette of four colours that could only ever be used one
way round would be a palette of four cards, and this show's look
is the pairing rather than any one of them.
Nothing stops the user setting white on white. That is not an
oversight either: the two lists are independent because the
pairing is the feature, and a rule barring the four matching
combinations would cost the panel more explaining than an
invisible caption costs the user, who can see it is invisible and
`text` reaches the highlight as well as the block - see the note
on `colors` in js/channels.js. This channel's highlight is a
different CUT of the face and not a different colour, so what
colour the type is has one answer and not two.
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Telegraf UltraBold, in the same colour as
the rest of the block. The highlight here is WEIGHT: the family's
two ends, 200 against 800, on the same card, which at this
contrast is as loud as a box would be and leaves the card one
clean shape instead of a shape with a second shape inside it.
The colour it names is the block's, so the recolour draws exactly
what its neighbours are drawn in and the face is the whole of the
difference. Stated all the same, for the fallback reason `color`
above is stated - a highlight that changed colour as well as
The mode and the scope come from the preset, which is where the
argument for picking out words rather than lines lives.
_comment_panel: Hot pink, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are
the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
It is the first entry in `colors.panel` above as well, so the
swatch that shows as chosen on an untouched frame is the one at
the start of the row. Nothing requires that - the swatch is found
by matching this value rather than by being listed first - and the
type's own colour is deliberately NOT first in its row, which is
the same freedom used the other way round.

_comment_branding: No dark gradient. It exists to hold a title legible against the
photograph, and this title is not against the photograph at all - it
is on a card of its own. A scrim over every still would darken forty
pictures to solve a problem the card has already solved.
